newsitem.title: USA: Congress must take responsibility for DC - Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Congress must take responsibility for DC - Gingrich.

text.p: Re-elected U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Tuesday that Congress needs to take on "our responsibility" to help the financially struggling District of Columbia.

"We should do it proudly, and we should not be ashamed to go back home and say you're darned right we are helping our national capital," said Gingrich, R-Ga., in a speech before the House of Representatives when he accepted the speakership.

House members should tell voters "We want you to visit (the District) with pride," Gingrich said. "We want you to know that you can say to anyone, anywhere in the world -- come to America and visit Washington. It is a great city."
Gingrich said Congress is beginning to make progress in aiding the city. "It is not easy. It has to be done carefully. It cannot violate the citizens of this city," he said.

"But let's be candid, this is our national capital," he added. "We have a unique obligation on both sides of the aisle to care about Washington because we are to Washington what a state government would be back home to your town."
Gingrich said some people thought "I had lost my mind" a year-and-a-half ago when he told D.C. Mayor Marion Barry that he wanted D.C. to be the "finest capital city in the world."
The speaker said he continues to believe that, in another statement that drew chamber applause.
He also said, "We owe it to every child of this District to have a decent chance to go to a school that succeeds in a neighborhood that is drug free and safe."
D.C.'s children should have "the expectation of getting a job in a community that actually cares about them and provides a better future," Gingrich said.
President Clinton said recently that the District's unusual status as a city without financial aide from a state has left it floundering in a "series of pergatories."
The Presidentis expected to announce plans for federal assistance to the city in his upcoming State of the Union address.
